items.title: Meta's Muse personal agent launches in the UK
items.summary: Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, is now available to anyone aged 18 and over in the UK on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp. You tell it a job, like chasing a refund or sorting the school calendar, and it can work across apps you connect, with UK partners such as Marks & Spencer, Currys, Trainline, Sainsbury's and easyJet. Meta says it is free for most of what people need, with optional paid plans for more usage, and it asks for your go-ahead before sending an email or making a purchase.
items.whyItMatters: Agents that do jobs for you are spreading across Europe's neighbours, but the post names the UK only, not Ireland. If you try any agent, check which apps you connect and keep approvals on for anything that spends money or sends messages.

items.title: ChatGPT's Chat tab gets GPT-6.2 for paid plans
items.summary: OpenAI is rolling out a version of GPT-6.2 tuned for everyday conversation in the ChatGPT Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users. OpenAI says it is better at following detailed instructions, finding information online and answering questions about images you share, and it can offer to tell you when a price drops. The models behind Work and Codex are not changing in this update.
items.whyItMatters: If you pay for ChatGPT, your normal chats should handle comparisons and photo questions better. The release note does not list the Free or Go plans.

items.title: Gemini for Mac can now use your computer for you (US, paid plans)
items.summary: Google added Computer use to the Gemini app for Mac. Gemini can click, type and fill in forms across desktop apps and websites in its own separate window, so you can watch, stop it with one click, or keep using your screen. You choose which apps it can use, and it pauses for logins or payments. It is rolling out in English for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US.
items.whyItMatters: It shows where AI assistants are heading: from answering to doing the clicking for you. It is not free and not yet outside the US.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a model that sits between Gemini 4 Hydrogen (fast everyday help) and Gemini 4 Carbon (the hardest projects). Google says it writes clearly, reads spreadsheets, PDFs and photos more precisely, and that Tasks in Gemini can now run on it. In the Gemini app it is for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, picked from the model drop-down; developers pay $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.
items.whyItMatters: If you pay for Gemini, you now have a faster middle option for reports and research. The post does not list it for free users.

items.title: ChatGPT Live Dictation rolls out to every plan
items.summary: OpenAI made dictation in ChatGPT faster: with Live Dictation your speech turns into text as you talk, instead of waiting for it to transcribe at the end. You can tap the waveform to show or hide the text as you go, and the old 10-minute recording limit is gone. It is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web and the desktop app.
items.whyItMatters: Talking is often easier than typing a long request. This works on the Free plan too, so you can ramble out what you need and let ChatGPT tidy it up.
